content_blocks.text: Overview
heading_path: Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication
Overview

content_blocks.text: This regulation permits contracting authorities to directly award contracts to, or negotiate contracts with, a particular supplier (a “direct award”) in the specific cases and circumstances set out in the regulation.
heading_path: Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication
Overview

content_blocks.text: There are three general grounds for making a direct award, four additional grounds relevant to public supply contracts only, an additional ground for making a direct award relevant to public service contracts that follow a design contest, and also a further additional ground for making a direct award relevant to new works or services which repeat similar ones.
heading_path: Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication
Overview

content_blocks.text: The regulation sets out the full rules and conditions for each of these grounds.
heading_path: Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication
Overview

content_blocks.text: Objective at this commercial stage
heading_path: Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication
Objective at this commercial stage

content_blocks.text: Direct awards are only permitted in accordance with the specific grounds set out in this regulation (i.e. regulation 32).
heading_path: Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication
Objective at this commercial stage

content_blocks.text: Contracting authorities should:
heading_path: Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication

content_blocks.text: consider whether any of the specific cases and circumstances set out in this regulation (i.e. regulation 32) apply, which could permit the contracting authority to make a direct award
heading_path: Use of negotiated procedure without prior publication
Key considerations at this commercial stage

content_blocks.text: ensure that the circumstances of the contract satisfy the relevant direct award ground before relying on it.
